meta.origin: Appalachian folk music, Old-Time, African-American blues; codified by Earl Scruggs in the 1940s (Bill Monroe's Blue Grass Boys)
meta.time_signature: 2/2 (cut time, written as 4/4 with half-note feel)
meta.typical_form: AABB (32-bar breakdown) or verse-chorus (V-C-V-C-B-C) with instrumental breaks interspersed
meta.mood: Driving, energetic, virtuosic; alternates between urgent forward motion and mournful high-lonesome balladry
reference_tracks: Bluegrass Breakdown - Bill Monroe & His Blue Grass Boys
Rawhide - Bill Monroe / Tony Rice Unit
Dueling Banjos - Eric Weissberg & Steve Mandell

pitch.name: Bluegrass Pentatonic / Mixolydian / Modal Hybrid
pitch.description: Bluegrass melody primarily uses the major pentatonic (G-A-B-D-E) with frequent Mixolydian flat-7 (F natural) and occasional blue note b3 (Bb). The G-run archetype in G major: G-A-B-D-E-F#-G (ascending) or G-F#-E-D-B-A-G (descending). Vocal-influenced bends and slides approximate the 'high lonesome' affect. The flatted 7th (F) is the most characteristic bluegrass scalar inflection, giving the music its modal Appalachian quality. Open-string drone (G-D-G-B-D banjo tuning) creates a constant pedal resonance.

characteristic_motifs.name: G-Run (ascending)
characteristic_motifs.description: Signature bluegrass lick: open G string (G3) → A → B → D → E → F# → G4. Often played as a scalar run on the banjo's 4th string or guitar bass run.

characteristic_motifs.name: G-Run (descending)
characteristic_motifs.description: Descending version: high G down through F#-E-D-B-A-G. Common turnaround figure at end of phrases.

characteristic_motifs.name: Blue Note Bend
characteristic_motifs.description: Bent b3 (Bb bent to B or B to C) sliding into root. Vocal-inspired, used on fiddle or banjo as a pull-off.

characteristic_motifs.name: Foggy Mountain Lick
characteristic_motifs.description: The iconic Foggy Mountain Breakdown riff: D5-E5-D5-B4-A4-F#4-D4. Descending pentatonic with forward-roll articulation.

rhythm.name: Scruggs Banjo Rolls (4/4 Cut Time)

variants.name: Forward Roll
variants.description: 5-3-1-5-3-1-5-3 string pattern (thumb-index-middle). The foundational Scruggs roll: continuous 8th-note flow with accents on thumb strokes (strings 5, 4, 3). Three fingers alternating in a forward cycle.

variants.name: Backward Roll
variants.description: 1-3-5-1-3-5-1-3 string pattern (middle-index-thumb). Reverse direction of forward roll. Used for descending scalar passages and phrase endings.

variants.name: Foggy Mountain Roll
variants.description: 5-3-1-5-3-1-3-1. Variation with doubled thumb stroke. Creates the signature syncopated drive of Foggy Mountain Breakdown. Accented thumb on beat 1, syncopated middle-index pair on offbeats.

variants.name: Alternating Thumb Roll
variants.description: 5-1-5-3-1-5-3-1. Thumb alternates between 5th and 3rd strings. Allows melodic notes on the open/fretted 5th string while maintaining roll pattern. Essential for melodic banjo style.

variants.name: Mandolin Chop (rhythm)
variants.description: Chop on beats 2 and 4 (backbeat). Mandolinist plays a muted strum on offbeats — the defining bluegrass rhythm guitar/mandolin punctuation.

variants.name: Bass Two-Beat (traditional)
variants.description: Root on beat 1, fifth on beat 3 (half-note feel). Walking bass lines use quarter-note scalar patterns between chord tones.

rhythm.time_feel: Driving eighth notes, straight (never swung), with a forward-pulling 'long-short' lift at moderate tempos. Cut time feel: two beats per bar felt strongly, with backbeat emphasis on 2 and 4.

timbre.harmonic_profile: bright, percussive attack with rapid decay; strong fundamental (1st) with prominent 2nd–5th harmonics; nasal midrange (1–2 kHz) from the head tension; metallic overtones from the tone ring (Mastertone style)

ornamentation.hammer_on: Left-hand hammer from lower to higher fret without picking — fills rapid 16th-note pairs between roll strokes
ornamentation.pull_off: Left-hand pull from higher to lower fret. Creates 'bounce' effect between repeating notes
ornamentation.slide: Fret-hand slide up or down to target pitch. Often on the 1st string for vocal-like bends
ornamentation.choke: Palm pressing bridge or head to raise pitch momentarily — 'scream' effect used on accent notes
ornamentation.roll_accent: Dynamic accent on thumb stroke (5th string) by picking harder — creates the characteristic driving pulse of Scruggs rolls

alternative_instruments.harmonic_profile: bright, cutting, with strong 3rd–6th harmonics; double-stops (open-string drones) create a full, bagpipe-like resonance
percussive 'chunk' on muted strings; bright, with quick decay; open string pairs produce a shimmering chorus effect
deep fundamental with warm 2nd–3rd harmonics; slap style adds percussive fingerboard impact at attack onset

unit_matrix.description: 2-bar Bluegrass Breakdown in G major, cut time (8 eighth-note slots per row). Tempo: 140 BPM. Grid represents one measure in 2/2 feel.

variations.name: Backward Roll Pattern (descending)
variations.description: Inverted Scruggs roll: middle-index-thumb cycle. Used for descending scalar passages (G-F#-E-D-B-A-G). Produces a softer attack profile than forward roll.

variations.name: Foggy Mountain Breakdown (syncopated thumb)
variations.description: Characteristic double-thumb accent pattern: 5-3-1-5-3-1-3-1. The delayed middle-index pair creates the signature syncopated drive. Tempo: 150 BPM.

variations.name: Waltz Time (3/4 bluegrass)
variations.description: Bluegrass waltz (3/4) with adapted rolls. Bass on 1, mandolin chop on 2 and 3. Banjo roll adjusts to 6 eighth notes per bar.

harmonic_progression.description: G (I) → C (IV) → D (V) → G (I). The I-IV-V progression with frequent V-of-V (A7 → D) and ii-V (Am-D7) substitutions. The flat-7 (F natural) in the Mixolydian mode allows the IV chord (C) to function as a subtonic when held. The V chord often incorporates the b7 (D7 → D7sus4 → D7) for a bluesy tension. Turnarounds typically use the 'G-run' over I → V7 → I progression.

cadences.deceptive: V → vi (D → Em) — less common, used in ballads
cadences.blues_turnaround: I → V-of-V → ii → V (G → A7 → Am → D7) — common in faster breakdowns

chord_voicings.mandolin_chop: Muted, percussive closed-position voicing (typically G4-B4-D5-G5, chopped on offbeats)

structural_rules: Breakdown form: AABB, each section 8 measures (32 total), repeated with variations
Each instrumental 'break' features a specific player taking the lead while others comp (chop rhythm + bass)
Banjo roll patterns are continuous eighth notes; breaks in the pattern signal phrase boundaries
G-run (ascending or descending scalar figure) typically ends each 8-bar section as a turnaround
Mandolin chop on beats 2 and 4 (backbeats) — never on 1 and 3 (except for accent at section starts)
Bass two-beat: root on 1, fifth on 3 (half-note feel) in traditional style; walking quarter notes in progressive style
Guitar provides bass runs (walking scalar lines between chord changes) + strummed rhythm on backbeats
Fiddle doubles melody at unison or third, adding double-stop drones and slides for Appalachian vocal quality
Tempo increases through each successive break (traditional 'razzing' or 'driving' effect)
Final chord is always the tonic (I) with an abrupt cutoff — no decay, ends with a 'snap'
No swing feel — straight eighth notes at all tempos
Open-string drone is structural: banjo's 5th string (high G) rings constantly, creating a pedal-point resonance
Accelerando through the breakdown: each repeat of AABB gets faster, building toward the final tag
